problem: Development throughput was repeatedly lost to queued or missing workflows, stale exact heads, broad false-positive test oracles, merge-base drift and duplicated recovery work. The system reacted after latency was already visible instead of admitting and supervising delivery proactively.
root_cause: The delivery system had strong safety gates but still behaved too much like a serial CI pipeline. Critical workflow admission could depend on ordinary PR triggering, the supervisor was primarily periodic, unrelated broad assurance could consume critical-path capacity, and parallel workers did not yet have a mandatory proof-capsule abstraction shared through one rolling candidate.
fix: Adopt a predictive proof-mesh instead of one serial pipeline.
Use event-driven PR/head admission to ensure Required and BRAIN start immediately; retain the scheduled supervisor only as watchdog fallback.
Detect partial critical-workflow starts and dispatch only the missing lane.
Use one rolling candidate per conflict contract while frontend, backend, QA, release and learning agents work in isolated parallel cells.
Require a proof capsule carrying identities, changed paths, contracts, dependencies, risk, blocking gates, targeted evidence and production-readback plan.
Move unrelated broad assurance into shadow/post-merge execution for bounded safe changes.
Never rebuild merely because main moved when there is no relevant overlap.
Treat queue, zero-run, partial-start, stale-run, timeout and merge-drift as recoverable delivery incidents.
Make regression oracles behavior/contract-specific to prevent incidental lexical false positives.
Feed timing, prediction error, conflicts, false positives, reruns, rollback and production outcomes back into daily gate/parallelism calibration.
scope_note: Current-main recovery keeps exact-head Required/BRAIN self-healing; turbo/gate-bypass proposals are explicitly excluded.
